title: Polynomial chaos stochastic collocation and galerkin uq

items.title: Finite product-law polynomial-chaos input data
items.strategy: Fix finitely many independent real inputs with product law, moment cutoffs, and positive-definite monomial Gram matrices; distinguish the finite construction from any completeness claim.

items.title: Completeness and spectral rates require law-specific hypotheses
items.strategy: Record the scope boundary: finite orthogonality follows from moments, while completeness and rates require separately proved density or mixed-regularity assumptions.

items.title: Total-degree and hyperbolic-cross chaos index sets
items.strategy: Define the total-degree and product hyperbolic-cross conventions explicitly, with the zero multi-index included.

items.title: Bochner L2 space for a finite product-law input
items.strategy: Define the strongly measurable, square-integrable V-valued equivalence classes and their integral inner product.

items.title: Positive moment Gram matrices produce orthonormal polynomial families
items.strategy: Use the positive monomial Gram matrix to prove independence in L2, then apply the finite Gram–Schmidt recursion and retain the leading-degree term.

items.title: Finite orthonormal polynomial tensor basis
items.strategy: Define each multivariate basis function as the product of the normalized one-dimensional polynomials indexed by the chosen finite set.

items.title: Uniformly elliptic affine random diffusion model
items.strategy: Specify the finite bounded input, measurable affine coefficient, uniform lower and upper bounds, conforming energy space, and square-integrable affine forcing.

items.title: The stated chaos index sets are finite and contain zero
items.strategy: Bound each coordinate of a multi-index by the declared total-degree or product threshold.

items.title: Finite-input Bochner L2 of a separable Hilbert space is Hilbert
items.strategy: Verify the integral pairing and prove completeness by selecting a summably Cauchy subsequence, taking its almost-everywhere Hilbert limit, and returning to L2 convergence.

items.title: Christoffel-weighted least-squares polynomial collocation
items.strategy: Specify the leverage density, reciprocal leverage weights, empirical Gram acceptance test, unique normal-equation solve, and unstable-sample status.

items.title: Finite polynomial-chaos orthogonal projection
items.strategy: Define each coefficient by the L2 pairing and the finite projection by the corresponding basis sum.

items.title: Affine diffusion forms are well-defined on Bochner L2
items.strategy: Prove measurability by simple-function approximation, establish L1 integrability by the uniform coefficient bound and Cauchy–Schwarz, and derive global boundedness and coercivity.

items.title: Independent polynomial-chaos tensor products are orthonormal
items.strategy: Factor each tensor inner product under the product law and use the one-dimensional orthonormality identities.

items.title: Quadrature estimates of polynomial-chaos coefficients
items.strategy: Define estimated coefficients by applying a declared cubature functional to each integrand u times its basis function.

items.title: Christoffel sampling is normalized and its weighted Gram has mean identity
items.strategy: Integrate the Christoffel kernel to the basis dimension, then compute the weighted rank-one matrix expectation and its leverage norm.

items.title: Affine random diffusion has a measurable Bochner solution
items.strategy: Apply pointwise Lax–Milgram, prove Lipschitz dependence by subtracting the affine variational equations, use the local Bochner form lemma, and extend the pointwise identity from dense simple tests.

items.title: Finite chaos projection, Parseval identity, mean, and variance
items.strategy: Prove residual orthogonality directly, apply Pythagoras, and separate the constant coefficient from the residual when computing variance.

items.title: Tensor products are dense in Bochner L2 under scalar and spatial density
items.strategy: Approximate by finite-valued simple functions, then approximate each scalar indicator in L2 by the assumed dense chaos span and each vector value by the assumed dense spatial subspace.

items.title: Projection and quadrature errors split in L2
items.strategy: Use residual orthogonality and Pythagoras to obtain the exact squared decomposition, then use the triangle inequality for the additive projection-plus-quadrature bound.

items.title: Bounded-Christoffel sampling stabilizes the empirical Gram matrix
items.strategy: Center the independent rank-one Gram summands, bound their norm and variance, apply the proved matrix Bernstein supplier, and simplify the constants to the declared sample budget.

items.title: Stochastic Galerkin coercivity and Cea quasi-optimality
items.strategy: Integrate the pointwise symmetric diffusion form over the product law, establish its exact coercivity and continuity constants, and apply the proved conforming Cea theorem on the finite tensor subspace.

items.title: Smolyak mixed-regularity bounds control chaos coefficient error
items.strategy: Apply the sparse-grid theorem separately to each coefficient integrand under its exact uniform-cube mixed-derivative assumptions, then combine the finite coefficient bounds in Euclidean norm.

items.title: Conditional spatial finite-element rate for stochastic Galerkin
items.strategy: Assume an exact finite chaos expansion with spatially regular coefficients; interpolate each coefficient conformingly, sum local H1 estimates by orthonormality, and apply stochastic Galerkin Céa.

items.title: Weighted least squares is stable on the good Gram event
items.strategy: Use the Gram eigenvalue interval to bound the pseudoinverse design map, then compare the fit with the L2 projection and the weighted sampled residual.

items.title: Tensor Gaussian rules recover polynomial-chaos coefficients exactly
items.strategy: Check the coordinatewise degree of each product integrand and apply the actual tensor Gaussian exactness theorem.

title: Polynomial chaos stochastic collocation and galerkin uq — Examples

items.title: A Cauchy input has no L2 degree-one polynomial chaos
items.strategy: Compute the divergent second moment of the standard Cauchy law and show the monomial Gram entry required for degree one is not finite.

items.title: Finite support can make a higher-degree moment Gram matrix singular
items.strategy: Use a nonzero polynomial vanishing on every support point to exhibit a nonzero coefficient vector in the Gram matrix kernel.

items.title: A bounded random diffusion coefficient remains uniformly coercive
items.strategy: For a uniform scalar input and an explicit affine positive coefficient, verify the pointwise bounds and the resulting energy coercivity.

items.title: A two-state uncertain reaction rate has an exact degree-one chaos expansion
items.strategy: Compute the two orthonormal modes on the symmetric two-point law, expand an affine reaction rate, and verify its mean, variance, and completeness on the two-point support.

items.title: Total-degree chaos uses fewer modes than a tensor product
items.strategy: Enumerate the three-dimensional degree-two multi-indices and compare the ten chaos modes with a three-by-three-by-three tensor Gaussian node count.
